usage_id.x-source: OB-004 depends on EV-001; an event needs a unique id. DECLARED INFERENCE from the Event Envelope, section 3.2.

occurred_at.x-source: Section 3.2 Event Envelope: occurred_at is a UTC timestamptz. DECLARED INFERENCE via OB-004's EV-001 dependency. BILLING IDENTITY DEPENDS ON THIS FIELD, recorded here at A6's request because the rule lived only in `dedupe_key` and in RFC-2026-014: this is the instant the measurement was TAKEN, stamped once and reused verbatim on every re-emission of that measurement. A producer that re-stamps on re-emission produces a different `dedupe_key` for one measurement, and the contract's own rule then sums it twice.

dimension.x-source: OB-004 Inputs names token / search / bytes / egress / processing / publish. Each value here RENAMES one of those to add its referent (`bytes` -> `storage_bytes`), which independent review correctly flagged: the mapping is one-to-one but the names are this contract's, not the task's.

amount.x-source: Carried as a decimal string for the same reason as money -- Decision Register 4.2 MOD-130. DECLARED INFERENCE that the prohibition extends to the number a cost is derived from. Bounded and leading-zero-free on the same grounds as cost.amount; an earlier draft said 'for the same reason' while permitting 60 fraction digits and unbounded magnitude, so the stated reason and the written pattern disagreed.

unit.x-source: DECLARED INFERENCE, previously UNSOURCED. OB-004's Inputs name token, search, bytes, egress, processing and publish; the UNITS those are counted in are not stated anywhere. `token`, `byte` and `second` follow from the dimensions; `request` and `operation` are this contract's own terms.

quantity.x-source: OB-004 requires money precision to be correct. A quantity is carried as a DECIMAL STRING for the same reason a money amount is; MOD-130 in Decision Register 4.2 forbids floating point for money. DECLARED INFERENCE that the rule extends to the quantity a cost is derived from.

attribution.x-source: OB-004 acceptance: 'workspace/business/job/provider attribution ครบ'. workspace, job and provider are required; business_profile_id is conditional because section 3.1 makes it conditional in the Tenant Context.

amount.x-source: OB-004 requires correct money precision; Decision Register 4.2 MOD-130 forbids floating-point money, so an amount is a decimal STRING. NO SIGN: an earlier draft allowed `-`, which would have materialized an explicitly OPEN decision -- NG-006 marks automated refund a non-goal, OPEN-001 leaves refund policy to Product and an accountant, and BILL-DEC-013 is Proposed. A credit must not enter this contract before that decision. PARSE AS ARBITRARY-PRECISION DECIMAL, NEVER AS A DOUBLE. CORRECTION, raised by A6 in co-owner review: an earlier version of this note justified the 16-digit integer bound as keeping a valid value inside IEEE-754 exact range. That was false -- `9999999999999999.99999999` is valid here and parses to 10000000000000000 as a double, past 2^53-1. The bound is a sane maximum, not a float-safety guarantee, and a consumer that parses these into a double loses money. Leading zeros are excluded so one amount has one spelling; note that scale is 2-8 digits, so `0.10` and `0.10000000` are one value with two spellings and no canonical form is stated yet. VAT treatment is absent by design and belongs to OPEN-001 with an accountant, not to this schema.

basis.x-source: DECLARED INFERENCE from OB-008, which reconciles usage against provider statements and so must know whether a figure was reported or estimated. A third value `list_price` was removed: it had no source and CONTRADICTED this package's own scope.exclude, which puts the provider price list out of scope. Independent review found the enum had three values where the stated inference yields two.

supersedes_usage_id.x-source: OB-008 reconciliation: a provider statement replaces an estimate. Without a reference to the estimate it supersedes, a reported event and the estimate it replaces are two events for one cost. DECLARED INFERENCE from OB-008; the task does not name the field. It is optional, so a first report with no prior estimate is expressible. CORRECTION, raised by A6 in co-owner review: an earlier version of this note claimed 'self-reference is rejected'. It is not, and it never was -- comparing two properties of one document is outside this validator's subset, so a document whose `cost.supersedes_usage_id` equals its own `usage_id` VALIDATES. Rejecting self-reference, and rejecting two events that supersede the same estimate, are resolver obligations; both are recorded under untestable_by_schema. A consumer must not build a fake on the strength of the old sentence.

cost.x-source: OB-004 requires correct money precision. A decimal STRING with an explicit scale, never a number: MOD-130 in Decision Register 4.2 forbids floating-point money. `basis` is a DECLARED INFERENCE from OB-008, which reconciles usage against provider statements and therefore needs to know whether a figure was reported or estimated.

dedupe_key.x-source: OB-008 detects missing and DUPLICATE usage, and ID-002 requires a dedupe record. COMPOSITION: `usg:<attribution.workspace_id>:<attribution.job_id>:<dimension>:<cost.basis>:<occurred_at>`, where the last segment is `occurred_at` reduced to DIGITS, `T` and a trailing `Z`. Precisely, and corrected after A6 demonstrated the earlier wording wrong: normalise `occurred_at` to UTC so it ends in `Z`, then drop `-`, `:` and the fraction's `.`; a fractional part is carried as its digits with no trailing zeros, and is omitted entirely when zero. `2026-08-31T10:00:00.123Z` gives `20260831T100000123Z`. The earlier wording said only "with its `-` and `:` removed", which leaves the `.` in place and produces a key this pattern REJECTS, and it said nothing about offsets, so a permitted `+07:00` composed to a key the pattern also rejects. A producer following that sentence literally was capped at SECOND resolution -- and one second is exactly the window in which the money-losing behaviour this key exists to prevent survives. WHAT THE KEY IDENTIFIES: one MEASUREMENT. Two events carrying the same key are the same measurement seen twice and the second is a duplicate; two measurements of the same job and dimension taken at different instants carry different keys and are SUMMED, not collapsed. WHY THE INSTANT IS IN THE KEY, recorded because an earlier version of this contract got it wrong and A6 refused to sign it: the composition first shipped as workspace/job/dimension/basis alone, together with the rule that a repeated key must be dropped. That instructed a consumer to DISCARD a second legitimate charge for the same job -- a job that makes two AI calls emits two real measurements -- and it manufactured exactly the double-count OB-008 exists to detect. Nothing in the baseline says a job emits one usage event per dimension, and this contract does not assert one. `cost.basis` stays in the key so a provider_reported correction is distinguishable from a duplicated estimate. REDELIVERY is a different problem with a different key: ID-002's inbox wrapper is keyed on the event id, which is `usage_id`, and N redeliveries of one event commit its effect once by that key, not by this one. That the key's parts MATCH this document's own fields is a resolver obligation the subset cannot express; see untestable_by_schema. Two distinct measurements recorded at the identical instant would collide, and are separated by `usage_id` rather than by this key. TWO DIRECTIONS, both recorded: two distinct measurements stamped with the identical instant collide and one is under-counted; one measurement re-emitted with a fresh timestamp carries a different key and is SUMMED, over-counting. The second direction was created by putting the instant in the key and is recorded here because A6 pointed out the limitation had been written in one direction only. Both are producer obligations: the instant is stamped once, at measurement, and reused on every re-emission.

tenant_context.x-source: Section 3.1: every command, query, job and event touching customer data carries the Trusted Tenant Context.
